narrative: bmad-epic-dev is a strong orchestration skill: lean activation, clear delegation to create-story / dev-story / code-review, and sensible parallelism constraints. The highest-impact improvements are (1) moving Step 0 and related YAML/table/DAG bookkeeping into a small pre-pass tool to cut tokens and variance, (2) fixing tooling/classification drift so multi-phase logic in references/ is not labeled a simple utility, and (3) reconciling automated commits and confirmation gates with common user policies via intent routing and commit modes.

broken.title: Automated workflow type contradicts multi-phase orchestration
broken.detail: workflow-integrity-prepass.json sets workflow_type to simple-utility while SKILL.md and references/phase-logic.md define validation, DAG planning, Phase A/C, completion, and resume—so automation may apply the wrong ruleset.
broken.action: Expose an explicit workflow classification in SKILL.md and/or teach the prepass classifier to detect phased logic living under references/*.md.

opportunities.name: Shift deterministic orchestration to pre-pass tooling
opportunities.description: YAML merges, epic discovery, markdown story-table parsing, DAG construction, layer grouping, sprint-status checks, and completion counts are mechanical but currently executed by the orchestrator LLM, driving heavy token use (roughly 1.3k–4.5k tokens per epic estimated shiftable) and parse/discovery failure modes.
opportunities.impact: Lower latency and token cost, more reliable structure, reusable JSON for scanners and CI validators, clearer halt messages when epic files are ambiguous.
opportunities.action: Add a PEP 723 Python or small CLI (single entrypoint with --help) that deep-merges BMad config, resolves the epic file, parses the Stories table, builds layers, emits epic_plan.json, and optionally runs post-step --verify assertions; update prompts to narrate that payload.

findings.title: Step 0 bundles epic resolution, YAML validation, table parse, DAG, and layers
findings.detail: Scanner estimates 500+ tokens of LLM tax per large run; work is deterministic graph/table/YAML logic.

findings.title: Config merge could emit resolved JSON instead of two-file reads
findings.detail: LLM loads _bmad/config.yaml and config.user.yaml separately; script could deep-merge and validate paths.

findings.title: Post–Phase A sprint-status verification is mechanical
findings.detail: Assert each story reached ready-for-dev after parallel create-story batch.

findings.title: Post–dev-story status check expects review state
findings.detail: Could be assert_status(epic, story, review) in tooling.

findings.title: New backlog detection after Phase C benefits snapshot diff
findings.detail: Avoid second full-file reasoning pass over sprint-status.yaml.

findings.title: Completion aggregates derivable from YAML/git
findings.detail: Counts of done stories and epic transitions can be scripted partially or fully.

findings.title: Resume routing table encodable in same module
findings.detail: Marginal token savings but fits bundled epic-plan tool.

findings.title: Optional extraction subagent/script threshold for huge epic markdown
findings.detail: Parent may ingest entire narrative body when only the Stories table matters.

findings.title: Epic file discovery heuristics can yield ambiguous matches
findings.detail: Needs explicit validation path: exactly one match, readable table, or templated halt.

opportunities.name: Harden phase reference against compaction and BMad conventions
opportunities.description: phase-logic.md is the executable prompt but omits a compact restatement of orchestration invariants, lacks explicit language/output headers, and lives outside numbered root stage files—so integrity tooling sees zero stages and context compaction can drop SKILL.md contract details.
opportunities.impact: Safer long-running epics, consistent triggering hooks, better automated checks, less cognitive friction from Phase A→C gap.
opportunities.action: Add a short anchor mirroring SKILL.md contract bullets; add communication/document-language preamble; shorten description hook; clarify Phase B; strengthen authoritative sequential-execution wording; document references-only pattern or split numbered stages.

findings.title: Missing anchor block for non-negotiable contract under compaction
findings.detail: Opening jumps into Step 0 without restating fresh subagents, relay decisions, halt/resume, sprint-status truth.

findings.title: No BMad-style config header binding communication_language
findings.detail: SKILL.md resolves variables but executable file lacks upfront binding.

findings.title: Complex-workflow checklist expects numbered root stage files
findings.detail: Single references/phase-logic.md diverges from 01-*.md convention.

findings.title: Missing explicit language/output preamble in phase reference
findings.detail: Scanner expects restated config-bound behavior for multi-step external prompts.

findings.title: Description first clause longer than 5–8 word hook
findings.detail: May dilute conservative triggering; shorten hook before Use when clause.

findings.title: Reference load instruction could state authoritative ordering
findings.detail: Add explicit execute-all-steps-in-order unless halted language.

findings.title: Phase lettering skips B between A and C
findings.detail: Readers assume missing content; note reserved or renumber.

opportunities.name: Align commits, intent routing, subagent contracts, and headless use
opportunities.description: Automated git commits conflict with common only-commit-when-asked rules; the flow lacks a lightweight wrong-skill guard before expensive parsing; subagent prompts omit structured completion payloads; experts and automators need fewer gates and explicit no-commit or JSON exit options.
opportunities.impact: Fewer expensive misfires, restored trust with cautious users, shorter handoffs, clearer path for CI or chained agents.
opportunities.action: Add intent-before-ingestion line with sibling skill pointers; introduce commit_policy modes; optional resume-silent or skip_confirmations when state implies Phase C only; define JSON or capped-bullet subagent return schema; document headless flags and minimal structured exit payload.

findings.title: Phase A and Phase C prescribe commits without user-rule reconciliation
findings.detail: Conflicts with workspace norms; needs explicit requirement or configurable deferral.

findings.title: No intent checkpoint before heavy epic parsing
findings.detail: Wrong skill invocation is costly; suggest confirming full-epic intent vs single-story.

findings.title: Commit policy should be first-class configuration
findings.detail: defer-commits or confirm-each-commit modes preserve checkpoints without silent conflict.

findings.title: Experts hit soft gates even when only Phase C remains
findings.detail: resume-silent or skip plan approval when sprint-status shows in-progress ready-for-dev only.

findings.title: Subagent prompts lack structured completion payload
findings.detail: Prose-only returns drive verbose handoffs and re-reads.

findings.title: Overview emphasis may over imply parallel implementation
findings.detail: Clarify parallelism applies to Phase A specs not Phase C implementation.

findings.title: Headless automation blocked by confirmations and relays
findings.detail: Needs documented auto-resolve parameters and structured exit JSON.

findings.title: create-story no-interaction wording vs relay-decisions contract
findings.detail: Align ambiguity handling with dev-story do-not-assume tone.

strengths.title: Lean activation and progressive disclosure
strengths.detail: SKILL.md stays ~33 lines (~458 tokens); long procedure lives in references/phase-logic.md without inline bloat.

strengths.title: Clear orchestrator vs implementer split
strengths.detail: Delegation to specialized BMad skills prevents role drift and keeps the parent focused on sequencing and checkpoints.

strengths.title: Concrete subagent templates
strengths.detail: Fenced prompts for create-story, dev-story, and code-review reduce improvisation errors.

strengths.title: Sound parallelism and checkpoint model
strengths.detail: Phase A parallelizes by DAG layer; Phase C stays sequential with rationale; sprint-status.yaml supports resume and amortizes rework.

strengths.title: Path and scaffold hygiene
strengths.detail: Path standards scan passed with zero findings; frontmatter naming matches folder; required sections present.

structure.assessment: Frontmatter, Overview, On Activation, and references wiring are correct; no orphaned placeholders or forbidden exit sections. Pre-pass automation under-classifies workflow type versus manual review.

craft.assessment: Overview quality is strong with appropriate length; rationale appears where procedure might be questioned; phase-logic behaves as the real stage prompt despite zero root *.md stage files in metrics.

cohesion.assessment: Coherent backlog-to-done identity with explicit loops for review-spawned stories; moderate tension between automated commits and typical user agent rules; skill-level workflow YAML graph absent by design.

stage_flow.notes: Validate and parse, plan, Phase A by layer, Phase C sequential, completion and spawn loop are explicit.

purpose_alignment.notes: Orchestrator role matches procedure; commit automation and confirmation density may mismatch user expectations.

complexity_appropriateness.notes: Single reference plus short activation fits full-epic scope; parallelism bounded with rationale.

completeness_gaps.notes: Epic discovery edge cases and git staging policy variance between phases remain underspecified.

redundancy.notes: SKILL.md vs phase-logic split avoids duplicated rules.

dependency_graph_logic.notes: Story DAG is well specified in prose; no machine-readable skill manifest for external runners.

external_skill_integration.notes: Clear chaining among create-story, dev-story, code-review with consistent halt semantics.

findings.title: git add scope differs between Phase A and Phase C
findings.detail: Phase A suggests broader adds vs Phase C git add -A; standardize with rationale.

findings.title: Optional structured workflow sidecar for future runners
findings.detail: Consider manifest mapping phases to inputs/outputs if BMad gains structured execution.

efficiency.assessment: Delegation-first design parallelizes independent spec work and serializes implementation intentionally; execution-deps prepass passes with empty stages because orchestration is markdown-driven.

experience.assessment: First-timers benefit from DAG education and resume contract but face opaque multi-epic backlog choice and commit discomfort; experts want fewer gates; edge cases need clearer discovery failure templates; automators need flags and JSON exits.

journeys.summary: Invocation works when one backlog epic exists; friction appears when multiple epics backlog, commits surprise users, or parsing fails late.
friction_points: Opaque epic selection when several backlog
Git commit assumptions vs personal rules
Late discovery of malformed story tables
bright_spots: Resume via sprint-status reduces fear of lost progress

journeys.summary: Wants Phase C throughput and minimal ceremony but hits confirmation prompts and sequential implementation constraint.
friction_points: Parallelism expectation mismatch from overview tone

journeys.summary: May trigger epic orchestration when meaning single-story work or PR review.
friction_points: No intent checkpoint before expensive Step 0
Risk of mutating wrong epic if misaligned
bright_spots: Epic done early exit is cheap when nothing remains

journeys.summary: Unusual paths include planning-only epic files, multi-deps strings, mid-flight stories, YAML drift, review-spawned backlog.
friction_points: Surprising loop back to Phase A after spawn
No spelled recovery for done marker vs missing artifacts
bright_spots: Re-parse DAG on resume handles partial completion

journeys.summary: Broken YAML, hook failures, read-only FS, or missing parallel subagents stress the flow.
friction_points: Unclear committed-vs-status state after git failures
No fallback if subagents unavailable entirely
bright_spots: Documented sequential fallback for Phase A when parallel blocked

journeys.summary: CI or chained agents want deterministic completion signals without human relays.
friction_points: No documented dry-run or no-commit contract
bright_spots: Externalized YAML and git state suit automation if gates parameterized

autonomous.notes: Checkpoint files help machines; human confirmations and relays remain blockers until parameterized.

findings.title: Optional epic distillate output for chaining agents
findings.detail: Low priority enhancement to invoke distillator or emit compact summary artifact.

scripts.assessment: No scripts directory exists; lint reports informational pass only. Highest ROI is bundling Step 0 with config merge into one epic-plan style tool plus optional validators.
scripts.token_savings: Roughly 1,300–4,500 tokens per full epic orchestration if mechanical steps move off-LLM (scanner estimate).

findings.title: scripts-temp scan found no scripts directory
findings.detail: Nothing to lint; opportunity is greenfield helper tooling.

recommendations.action: Implement epic-plan / bmad-context pre-pass emitting epic_plan.json and fix workflow-type classification for references-based phased skills.
Add phase-logic anchor block, language preamble, shorter description hook, Phase B note, and stronger authoritative execution wording.
Introduce intent-before-ingestion gate plus commit_policy modes and optional resume-silent or skip_confirmations behaviors.
Define structured subagent completion schema for create-story, dev-story, and code-review handoffs.
Clarify in Overview that parallelism applies to Phase A specs while Phase C implementation stays sequential per branch.
Standardize git staging policy across Phase A and Phase C with one sentence of rationale.
